## Description

The classic giant amoeba of ponds (here ~180 µm). It extends lobose pseudopods, engulfs algae and
ciliates with its membrane and encloses them in food vacuoles. It has a single nucleus and a
contractile vacuole.

## In the simulation

<!-- GENERATED:presence -->
Drops: `moss` (weight 0.5), `pond` (weight 0.15), `puddle` (weight 0.15); 2 individuals in a reference drop at weight 1.
<!-- /GENERATED -->

Plastic membrane without shape memory: pseudopods emerge from cortical tension and membrane
remeshing. It is the reference being for the [phagocytic cup](../../mechanics/feeding-and-phagocytosis.md) (zipper
mechanism) and can be controlled with click-and-drag pseudopods. Contractile vacuole period in fresh
water estimated.

## Literature

- Rogerson A. (1980) Can. J. Zool.: generation time of *A. proteus* fed *Tetrahymena pyriformis*,
  44 h at 20 °C (Rogerson 1978 thesis, Univ. of Stirling: 44–84 h depending on food).
- Stock C., Grønlien H.K., Allen R.D., Naitoh Y. (2002) J. Exp. Biol. 205: 1171 (cytosol osmolarity
  of *Paramecium*, used as an order of magnitude).

## Not implemented yet

- Its µmax with *Tetrahymena* as prey is not validated (needs a culture with abundant ciliate prey;
  roadmap B).
- No dependence on endosymbiotic bacteria (Jeon 1972).
- Pseudopod dynamics (sol–gel conversion, uroid) are emergent approximations.

## Unique and shared mechanics

Defines the [plastic membrane](../../mechanics/soft-bodies.md#plastic-membrane-amoebae) and the
[phagocytic cup](../../mechanics/feeding-and-phagocytosis.md#phagocytic-cup-zipper-mechanism) shared by every
amoeba and the neutrophil; [contractile vacuole cycle](../../mechanics/genome-and-organelles.md).
